stem:
Damini checks which expression must always be even for integer values of the letters. She compares $6a + 2b$ with $n^{2} + 1$.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: $6a + 2b$ is always even only when $a$ and $b$ are even.
Integer values of the letters are produced by an expression being even.
$6a + 2b$ must always be even, while $n^{2} + 1$ is not always even.
$n^{2} + 1$ must always be even because the constant $1$ sits next to a square.

teacher.key_rationale: 6a+2b=2(3a+b) is always even for integers a,b. n^2+1 is odd when n is even, so it is not always even. Restricting to even letters, reversing cause, or trusting the constant beside a square, miss the factor-of-2 test.
